correctness.rationale: All quantities, event domains, and zero-boundaries were checked. Weighted bipartite tree degree enumerator gives independent classwise multinomial degree arrays. A derived weighted electrical-resistance identity yields the marked-edge moment. The exact cross-class and within-class covariance matrix follows by conditional orientation probabilities. Strict balanced definiteness is a one-variable power inequality; fixed-side indefinite limiting determinant has controlled binomial expansions. K2,4 positive witness equals 191/4096 and exact enumeration verified nine pairs up to K4,4 with 92 assertion groups; finite tests do not prove all sizes.

originality.rationale: A source–sink event for adjacent vertices has twice the conditional nonadjacent orientation probability. A complete-bipartite random tree requires the edge-marked nonlinear degree moment, yielding a positive cross-class covariance but negative within-class covariance. The resulting 2x2 part-covariance matrix has a provable balance-dependent inertia change, not supplied by fixed-tree extremal comparisons, edge-indicator covariances, or separate degree-array independence. Exact literature and indexed-record comparisons do not show a dominating earlier formulation. Priority remains qualified, rather than established by unsuccessful searches.
residual_risks: Published UST and oriented-tree literature beyond inspected full texts might contain an equivalent partwise covariance computation, especially in work using graph reliability or random orientations.

The marked-edge calculation is a relatively short synthesis of known weighted matrix-tree and transfer-current tools; priority of its explicit sign consequence merits independent literature verification.

value.rationale: This is a natural source-versus-sink dependence question for directed networks sampled via random spanning trees. Its exact partwise covariance resolves whether every identical class weighting produces repulsion: yes for balanced K_{m,m} (m≥3), no for any fixed side a≥2 at sufficiently large imbalance. The explicit K2,4 positive direction and all-size negative-to-indefinite matrix signature describe a motivated structural distinction beyond a small numerical or textbook exercise.
